proposal.thesis: Parker Hannifin reported record fiscal Q4 2026 results on ~2026-08-06/07: record quarterly sales of $5.8B (+9.8%), adjusted segment operating margin 28.0% (+110bps), and adjusted EPS $9.27 (+21%), all quarterly records (WebSearch: Yahoo Finance, Quiverquant, TipRanks earnings-call coverage). Full fiscal-2026 results were also records: sales >$21.5B, organic growth 6.6%, adjusted EPS $32.31 (+18%), operating cash flow $4.4B. Management issued FY2027 guidance of 5.5-8.5% reported sales growth (7% midpoint), adjusted segment operating margin ~27.7% at midpoint, and adjusted EPS $34.75 at midpoint, and set a new FY2031 long-term adjusted segment margin target of 30% (+300bps from current record levels) -- while pursuing the pending Filtration Group and CIRCOR acquisitions. In the bundle, PH ranks in the top_setups lane (score 6.37), sits in the post_print_drift preferred lane (5 days since earnings, gap_held_revisions_up with 92% of the gap retained), carries a rising 30-week MA and uptrend weekly structure, and reports again in 85 days -- safely outside any earnings window for this swing. Digest fundamentals (quarter ended 2026-03-31 basis pre-print, now superseded by the fresh print above): revenue $5.486B +15.7% YoY, net income $904M, FCF $3.678B, net_debt_to_ebitda 1.67x (moderate), no discretionary insider activity either direction. Unlike today's other scanner leaders (NET, RBRK, MPC, AXON), which all popped another 4-9% intraday on top of an already large prior move, PH is essentially flat today (+0.36% intraday vs yesterday's close) -- this is a non-chasing entry into a fresh (2-session-old) post-earnings base, not a momentum chase.
catalysts: Record FY2026 Q4 results (adj EPS $9.27 +21%, record 28.0% segment margin) and FY2027 guidance (5.5-8.5% sales growth, $34.75 midpoint adj EPS), reported ~2026-08-06/07
New FY2031 long-term adjusted segment operating margin target of 30% (+300bps from current record levels), announced same call, plus pending Filtration Group and CIRCOR acquisitions

Wave of analyst price-target increases this week: Truist to $1,358, BMO to $1,214, UBS to $1,250, Citi to $1,232, KeyBanc to $1,210 (WebSearch-verified, not in bundle; bundle's cached mean target is $1,148.95)
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive (SPY above its 200-DMA, regime_hint 4/5) with momentum_health healthy (no factor unwind) and broad universe breadth constructive (74.7% of the universe above its 200-DMA, A/D 1.34). consumer_industrial_leaders is one of the accelerating sectors over the last month (sector_rotation_30d +6.1pp) while PH itself is flat intraday today, unlike several richer, more extended scanner leaders (NET, RBRK, MPC, AXON) that each popped another 4-9% today. One live macro flag: rising 10-year yields (4.65%, +27bp over 3 months) are a mild headwind for premium industrial multiples, though PH's real FCF and record margins offset pure duration risk better than an unprofitable grower would. The current book carries zero consumer_industrial exposure (BKR=energy, DXCM=healthcare, HPE=hyperscaler_server_capex), so this is a genuine fourth, uncorrelated leg (corr_to_book 0.09, beta 0.69 per portfolio_risk) rather than doubling an existing bet.
proposal.risk_map: This fails if (1) the FY2027 guide proves conservative-in-name-only and Q1 FY27 organic growth undershoots the 5.5% low end -- PH's premium (fwd P/E ~27.8x, 17th-of-18-cheapest in its own sector comp set) has little room for a growth disappointment; (2) the Filtration Group/CIRCOR deals face integration or regulatory delay, removing the M&A growth leg the raised long-term margin target assumes; (3) this is a fresh post-earnings level with only 2 sessions of base-building -- the freshly-raised analyst-target wave could fade if it doesn't hold over the next 1-2 weeks, or if the broader industrial tape rolls over; (4) rising 10-year yields (4.65%, up from 4.38% three months ago) pressure industrial/duration-sensitive multiples broadly, independent of PH's own execution. Early tell: a daily close back below $1,015 on rising volume, or the fresh $1,200+ analyst targets failing to hold/getting walked back over the next 1-2 weeks.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: the Street's cached mean target sits near $1,032-1,148 (bundle target_mean_price $1,148.95, itself already a touch stale relative to this week's news), reflecting Parker Hannifin as a steady, unexciting industrial compounder growing high-single-digits. MY VIEW: the market has not yet fully repriced the record FY2026 Q4 beat (adjusted EPS $9.27, +21%, record 28.0% segment margin) and the FY2027 guide alongside the newly-raised FY2031 long-term margin target (+300bps) and the pending Filtration Group/CIRCOR deals. MECHANISM: sell-side coverage lags the 2026-08-06/07 print -- Truist, BMO, UBS, Citi and KeyBanc have already moved targets to $1,210-1,358 this week (WebSearch-verified), well above the bundle's cached $1,148.95 mean, meaning the visible consensus figure understates where coverage is actually converging. RESOLUTION: watch for remaining coverage (JPMorgan still at a more conservative $1,140) to catch up over the next 2-4 weeks, and for the FY2027 Q1 print (~November 2026) to confirm the margin trajectory the new targets assume.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: FY2027 Q1 results (due ~November 2026) showing organic sales growth below the 5.5% guided low end, or adjusted segment operating margin falling below the 27.7% FY27 midpoint guide.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below $1,015 -- below the structural stop and the post-earnings gap's support -- on above-average volume, invalidating the post-print base.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If PH has not reclaimed and closed above $1,100 within 40 trading days of entry (roughly mid-October 2026), the fresh-analyst-target repricing thesis isn't playing out -- exit and rotate.
